summary.plain: A stack of camera-sensor-like silicon chips, cooled and shielded two kilometres underground at SNOLAB, watching for the faint trace of a dark matter particle bumping into a silicon atom.
summary.technical: CCD array: seven 16-Mpixel CCDs (6.0 g each, ~42 g total) in the 2017-2018 SNOLAB run (11 kg-day exposure); later replaced/supplemented by two 24-Mpixel skipper CCDs for a low-energy-threshold run through at least January 2024. Per a 2025 SNOLAB workshop report, the detector has since been repurposed as a background test stand.

technology.value: Thick, fully-depleted scientific CCDs for ionization detection, later supplemented with skipper-readout CCDs for single-electron sensitivity
